answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded by compliance regardless of memory_b1's apparent success, so that memory isn't actionable here. The live signal—write-path p99 climbing over 90 minutes, confined to primary region, coinciding with peak settlement write volume—most resembles the capacity-exhaustion pattern in memory_b3 rather than the discrete-dependency-failure pattern in memory_b1 or the partner-outage pattern behind circuit breaking. Regional failover (memory_b2) is tempting because it fixed a latency degradation before, but that record doesn't establish it was write-safe under heavy transactional load; shifting write traffic across regions during a settlement peak risks split-brain or dropped writes, which directly conflicts with the primary objective of not losing customer writes. I want to verify memory_b3 to confirm the prior capacity add specifically relieved write-path pressure (not just read/queue metrics) and verify memory_b2 to check whether that failover event involved write traffic or was read/latency-only, since that changes the risk calculus substantially. Circuit breaking and read-replica routing don't match this failure shape (no external dependency failure, and the problem is primary-region writes, not report-query load), so those memories aren't spent on verification. Pending verification, add_capacity is the intervention least likely to jeopardize write durability while still targeting the resource-pressure signal, so I'm proceeding as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout given the single-shot constraint and residual uncertainty about root cause.
